entries.Quote: "Meryl Streep is the benchmark against which all other actors are measured."
"For some reason, I have WWE wrestlers tweeting me all the time. Why they can connect with my love for Meryl Streep, I don't know."
"Know who you are, because that's how you will be cast at first. Then you can be Meryl Streep further down the road."
"I've always wanted to be a Meryl Streep or a Natalie Portman. I want to do all kinds of different movies, to be a chameleon."
"As far as actresses go, I love Meryl Streep."
"I guess if they ever do a remake of Sophie's Choice, I could play the Meryl Streep part. I've got to work on my Polish accent."
"Everything we say signifies; everything counts, that we put out into the world. It impacts on kids, it impacts on the zeitgeist of the time."
"Pretending is not just play. Pretending is imagined possibility. It is a very valuable life skill and we do it all the time."
"Listening is everything. Listening is the whole deal. With your children, with your husband, with your friends, with your mother, with your father."
"True freedom is understanding that we have a choice in who and what we allow to have power over us."
"Streep was awarded the AFI Life Achievement Award in 2004."
"She received the Kennedy Center Honor in 2011 for her contribution to American culture."
"In 2017, her lifetime of achievement was honored at the Golden Globes with the Cecil B. DeMille Award."
"She was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Obama in 2014."
"She was awarded the National Medal of Arts by President Obama in 2010."
"Streep made her stage debut in Trelawny of the Wells and received a Tony nomination for her first Broadway roles in 1976."
"She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for Kramer vs. Kramer in 1979 — her first Oscar."
"She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for Sophie's Choice in 1982 and The Iron Lady in 2011."
"Young people who learn the arts do better in every phase of their lives."
"You don't have to be famous. You just have to make your mother and father proud of you."
"I think there's a great worth in what we do. Giving voice to characters that have no other voice."
"I had a number of great teachers and the ones that really were the strongest influences on me were women."
"Being a celebrity has taught me to hide, but being an actor has opened my soul."
"I think the most liberating thing I did early on was to free myself from any concern with my looks as they pertained to my work."
"I never look a gift horse in the mouth. My career has been given to me by the people I've worked with."
"People want what they want. Sometimes you just have to walk in defiance of it and just be yourself."
"I would like to thank BAFTA for this wonderful honor, I would like to spank — [horrified look] — thank Spike Jonze..."
"Let's face it, we were all once 3-year-olds who stood in the middle of the living room and everybody thought we were so adorable. Only some of us grow up and get paid for it."
"It's bizarre that the produce manager is more important to my children's health than the pediatrician."
"Wrinkled, wrinkled little star... hope they never see the scars."
"The interesting thing about being a mother is that everyone wants pets, but no one but me cleans the kitty litter."
"Florals? For spring? Groundbreaking."
entries.Context: The Devil Wears Prada (2006) — her most quoted film line

entries.Quote / Moment: "Holy mackerel!"
entries.Context: First Oscar win — Kramer vs. Kramer (1980) — opening words

entries.Quote / Moment: "When they called my name I had this feeling I could hear half of America going, 'Oh no. Oh, c'mon — why? Her? Again?' But, whatever."
entries.Context: Third Oscar — The Iron Lady (2012) — opening

entries.Quote / Moment: "First I'm going to thank Don, because when you thank your husband at the end of the speech they play him out with the music."
entries.Context: Oscar speech (2012) — on her husband Don Gummer

entries.Quote / Moment: "Everything I value most in our lives, you've given me."
"Thirty-seven years ago, my first play in New York City, I met the great hairstylist and makeup artist Roy Helland. Every single movie in between."
entries.Context: Oscar speech (2012) — on her longest collaborator

entries.Quote / Moment: "I want to thank my colleagues for the work that has brought such inspiration and joy to my life."
"I had a wonderful time making this movie. And I want to thank the Academy for this incredible honor."
entries.Context: Oscar acceptance — characteristic brevity and warmth

entries.Quote / Moment: "I want to thank my amazing partners in this enterprise."
entries.Context: Oscar speech pattern — always credits collaborators first

entries.Quote / Moment: She holds the record for the most Academy Award nominations of any actor — 21.
entries.Context: Career fact — unmatched in Oscar history

entries.Quote / Moment: Three wins: Kramer vs. Kramer (1980), Sophie's Choice (1983), The Iron Lady (2012).
She has been nominated in all but twelve years since 1979.
Her first nomination came for The Deer Hunter in 1978, just one year after her film debut.
She won Best Supporting Actress before Best Actress — showing range from the very start.
entries.Context: Career fact — Kramer vs. Kramer (Supporting) then Sophie's Choice (Lead)

entries.Quote / Moment: Between her first and third Oscar, thirty-two years passed — proof that greatness doesn't expire.
"I've been nominated 789 times and I was getting settled over there for a long winter's nap."
"It hasn't been since the Pleistocene Era that I won anything."
"I think I've worked with everybody in the room! I have!"
entries.Context: Golden Globe win for The Devil Wears Prada (2007)

entries.Quote / Moment: "Oh shut up, it's not that long."
entries.Context: Golden Globe speech (2007) — silencing a groaner when she pulled out notes

entries.Quote / Moment: "I just realized you can see completely through my dress."
entries.Context: Golden Globe win for Angels in America (2004) — opening line

entries.Quote / Moment: "I just wanna say that I don't think the two biggest problems in America are that too many people wanna commit their lives to one another and steroids in sports."
entries.Context: Golden Globe speech (2004) — rare political moment

entries.Quote / Moment: "This is the greatest award because it throws it in the teeth of the critics."
entries.Context: National Movie Award for Mamma Mia! (2008) — shading the critics

entries.Quote / Moment: "Sh... it! I forgot my glasses."
entries.Context: Golden Globe win for The Iron Lady (2012) — the un-bleeped moment

entries.Quote / Moment: With 30 Golden Globe nominations and 8 wins, she holds both records for any actor in history.
"Harvey Weinstein passes the glasses to George Clooney, who passes them to David Fincher, who completely drops the ball."
entries.Context: Golden Globe (2012) — the glasses relay incident

entries.Quote / Moment: "My mother shared Julia Child's verve. She had a real joy in living and no patience for gloom and doom. I'm not like that."
entries.Context: Golden Globe win for Julie & Julia (2010)

entries.Quote / Moment: "I come to Golden Globes weekend and I am honestly conflicted how to have my happy movie self in the face of everything I'm aware of in the real world."
entries.Context: Golden Globe speech (2010) — on the tension between celebration and reality

entries.Quote / Moment: "Partners in Health. Shoot some money to Partners in Health. Put the dress on. Put on a smile and be damn grateful."
entries.Context: Golden Globe (2010) — channeling her mother's voice

entries.Quote / Moment: "Hollywood is crawling with outsiders and foreigners. And if you kick them all out, you'll have nothing to watch but football and mixed martial arts."
entries.Context: Cecil B. DeMille speech (2017) — on diversity

entries.Quote / Moment: "There are some days when I, myself, think I'm overrated. But not today."
entries.Context: Emmy win for Angels in America (2004) — possibly her most quoted speech line

entries.Quote / Moment: "Oh, and I can sing this just as well."
entries.Context: Emmy speech (2004) — when the orchestra tried to play her off

entries.Quote / Moment: "Glenn Close is my friend so I know she'll forgive me. Helen Mirren is an acting god. Emma Thompson will hold a grudge for the rest of her life. But who cares?"
entries.Context: Emmy speech (2004) — ribbing her fellow nominees

entries.Quote / Moment: "And, can I just say, there is no such thing as the Best Actress. There is no such thing as the greatest living actress."
entries.Context: SAG Award for Doubt — characteristic humility

entries.Quote / Moment: "Streepeeches are truly works of art. They're as good as the performances she wins them for."
entries.Context: TV Guide editorial — on her speeches as an art form

entries.Quote / Moment: "One day, they'll give out an award for speeches and call it the Streep."
entries.Context: TV Guide — on her speech-giving legacy

entries.Quote / Moment: She handles being played off with aplomb every time — sometimes singing, sometimes ignoring, always winning.
entries.Context: Press observation — on her orchestra battles

entries.Quote / Moment: Her speeches are clever, funny, daffy, self-effacing, appreciative, all delivered with perfect timing.
"Hollywood, foreigners, and the press — the most vilified segments in American society right now."
entries.Context: Opening framing — Cecil B. DeMille speech

entries.Quote / Moment: "But who are we, and what is Hollywood anyway? It's just a bunch of people from other places."
"Viola was born in a sharecropper's cabin in South Carolina. Sarah Paulson was raised by a single mom in Brooklyn. Amy Adams was born in Italy. Natalie Portman was born in Jerusalem."
"Ryan Gosling, like all the nicest people, is Canadian."
"If you kick them all out, you'll have nothing to watch but football and mixed martial arts, which are not the arts."
"This instinct to humiliate, when it's modeled by someone powerful, filters down into everybody's life, because it gives permission for other people to do the same thing."
entries.Context: On the dangers of cruelty from power

entries.Quote / Moment: "Disrespect invites disrespect. Violence incites violence. When the powerful use their position to bully others, we all lose."
entries.Context: The most quoted lines from the speech

entries.Quote / Moment: "We need the principled press to hold power to account, to call them on the carpet for every outrage."
"That's why our founders enshrined the press and its freedoms in our Constitution."
"Tommy Lee Jones said to me, 'Isn't it such a privilege, Meryl, just to be an actor?' Yeah, it is."
"We have to remind each other of the privilege and the responsibility of the act of empathy."
As my friend, the dear departed Princess Leia, said to me once: take your broken heart, make it into art.
That speech would go viral, played and replayed by tens of millions.
entries.Context: Lorenzo Soria (HFPA President) — on the speech's impact

entries.Quote / Moment: Trump tweeted calling Meryl 'over-rated,' which only helped bring even more attention to the speech.
"This is your time and it feels normal to you, but really there is no normal. There's only change and resistance to it and then more change."
"Pretending is not just play. Pretending is imagined possibility."
"I think your self emerges more clearly over time. In the end, it's what feels right to you — the still, small voice."
"I would like to thank BAFTA for this wonderful honor, I would like to spank — [horrified look] — thank Spike Jonze..."
entries.Context: BAFTA ceremony — the famous Freudian slip

entries.Quote / Moment: "I think children are reflections of the people who raise them. The fact that Meryl has played both parts so well, as an actress and as a mother, makes her such an icon."
entries.Context: Her son presenting her Honorary Golden Bear in Berlin

entries.Quote / Moment: "If it doesn't, I don't care, she's still the best there is."
entries.Context: Her son — concluding his Berlin tribute

entries.Quote / Moment: She was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Obama in 2014 — the nation's highest civilian honor.
She received the Kennedy Center Honor in 2011 for her contribution to American culture through performing arts.
She was awarded the AFI Life Achievement Award in 2004 — one of the youngest recipients in the award's history.
"Listening is everything. Listening is the whole deal."
entries.Context: Public remarks — on what matters most

entries.Quote / Moment: She stares. That's the first thing you notice about her.
She is an observer and a thief. She reveals what she has stolen on that sacred place which is the screen.
She makes the most heroic characters vulnerable, the most known familiar, the most despised relatable.
Her artistry reminds us of the impact of what it means to be an artist, which is to make us feel less alone.
"I can only imagine where you go, Meryl, when you disappear into a character. I imagine that you are in them, patiently waiting, using yourself as a conduit."
"You make me proud to be an artist. You make me feel that what I have in me — my body, my face, my age — is enough."
entries.Context: Viola Davis — Golden Globe tribute — the climax

entries.Quote / Moment: "Every day my husband would call me at night and say, 'Did you tell her how much she means to you?' And I would say, nah, I can't say anything."
entries.Context: Viola Davis — on filming Doubt together

entries.Quote / Moment: "I see you. I see you."
entries.Context: Viola Davis — the emotional peak of the tribute

entries.Quote / Moment: Miranda Priestly's withering glances in The Devil Wears Prada became a language unto themselves — more was said in a look than most actors convey in a monologue.
entries.Context: The Devil Wears Prada (2006) — written by Aline Brosh McKenna

entries.Quote / Moment: She changed 'Everybody wants to be me' to 'Everybody wants to be us' at the table read — a single word that transformed the entire character.
entries.Context: The Devil Wears Prada — Streep's own contribution

entries.Quote / Moment: Her exclamation about a dingo and her baby, delivered in a flawless Australian accent, became embedded in pop culture for decades.
entries.Context: A Cry in the Dark (1988) — widely referenced on Seinfeld

entries.Quote / Moment: "I have doubts. I have such doubts."
entries.Context: Doubt (2008) — the devastating final line, written by John Patrick Shanley

entries.Quote / Moment: Her portrayal of Julia Child's breathy enthusiasm was so precise that critics said she didn't play Child — she channeled her.
entries.Context: Julie & Julia (2009) — written by Nora Ephron

entries.Quote / Moment: Sophie's impossible choice remains one of cinema's most harrowing scenes — Streep reportedly could only film it in a single take.
entries.Context: Sophie's Choice (1982) — written by Alan J. Pakula

entries.Quote / Moment: As Margaret Thatcher, she spent months studying voice recordings, body language, and notecards Thatcher carried with quotes from Lincoln and Shakespeare.
She needed much more breath than her drama school training gave her to match Thatcher's vocal stamina at age 65.
entries.Context: The Iron Lady — on Thatcher's vocal power

entries.Quote / Moment: In Kramer vs. Kramer, her courtroom breakdown sealed her first Oscar and redefined how custody battles were portrayed on screen.
entries.Context: Kramer vs. Kramer (1979) — written by Robert Benton

entries.Quote / Moment: Karen Silkwood's final drive down a dark highway remains one of the most unsettling endings in film — Streep made the mundane terrifying.
As the Witch in Into the Woods, she proved at 65 that she could carry a Sondheim musical on screen with full vocal authority.
entries.Context: Into the Woods (2014) — Stephen Sondheim score

entries.Quote / Moment: In Big Little Lies, her quiet menace as Mary Louise Wright earned her a fourth Emmy nomination — proving television was no step down.
